title: 1987 AMC 8 Problem 25
statement: Ten balls numbered \(1\) to \(10\) are in a jar. Jack reaches into the jar and randomly removes one of the balls. Then Jill reaches into the jar and randomly removes a different ball. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers on the balls removed is even?

solutions.text:
The sum is even when both balls are odd or both are even. There are \(\binom{5}{2} = 10\) all-odd pairs and \(\binom{5}{2} = 10\) all-even pairs, for \(20\) favorable pairs.

The total number of pairs is \(\binom{10}{2} = 45,\) so the probability is \(\dfrac{20}{45} = \dfrac49.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: The sum of two numbers is even exactly when both are odd or both are even
There are \(5\) odd and \(5\) even balls; count the matching-parity pairs out of all \(\binom{10}{2}\) pairs
